P0_population.description: The audited population: every suspect tail with mark=='copied' whose tail is not in any of the 38 already-flagged theory groups. 12760 tails carry mark 'copied'; the 38 groups cover 1292 tails of which only 530 are 'copied', so 12230 remain. Max fan-out is 3 new keys; every tail has exactly one old record; the constituent symmetric difference is never empty; and every one of the 12230 contains a cross-key pair of theories that share a base name whose source-file token-set Jaccard is >= 0.30 -- i.e. my reimplementation of the existing filter reproduces it exactly and fires on none of them.

P1_no_shared_base_name_pair.description: CANDIDATE RULED OUT (empty). Tails whose constituent symmetric difference contains no cross-key pair of theories sharing a base name -- the case the existing filter structurally cannot see. There are none: for a tail to exist the printed proposition must be identical in both claimants, which forces the differing constituent to be a same-base-name duplicate of a theory. Only 136 distinct differing theory pairs generate all 12230 tails.
P1_no_shared_base_name_pair.query: for each tail: D = union(constituents) - intersection(constituents); pairs = {(a,b) in D x D, a from one key's set only, b from another's only, basename(a)==basename(b)}; select pairs == {}

P2_text_names_a_single_claimant.description: CANDIDATE RULED OUT (empty). Tails whose stored English contains, as a whole word, a theory long name or session name that belongs to exactly one claimant. Zero. 367 of the 12230 do mention a claimant theory token (top: Word 91, List 69, Sigma 61, DiningPhilosophers 36, NodeClass 22) but the token is always the shared BASE name, which by construction belongs to every claimant; no interpretation in this population ever names a session (no 'Zip_Benchmarks', 'Incompleteness', 'Core_SC_DOM', ...). The deformalizer writes about the proposition, not about where it lives, so this heuristic has no purchase here.
P2_text_names_a_single_claimant.query: for each tail: ids(key) = {theory longname} u {session prefix} over claimants and constituents; uniq(key) = ids(key) - union(ids(other keys)); select any tok in uniq(key), len>=4, matching /(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])tok(?![A-Za-z0-9_])/ in interpretation

P3_fanout_3.description: Tails where one old English went onto 3 new keys instead of 2. All 267 are the same single situation: the HOL-MicroJava dataflow-analysis library (DFA/Semilat, Listn, Err, Opt, Product, LBVSpec, Kildall, Typing_Framework*) vendored into both Jinja and JinjaThreads, so MicroJava/Jinja/JinjaThreads all claim the fact. Adjudicated clean: the three copies state the affected lemmas verbatim.

examples.interpretation: This rule obtains a comparison with a top element. If `T` is a top element for the relation `r`, then for any value `x` the rule establishes `x ⊑⇘r⇙ T`, meaning that `r` relates `x` to `T`.

P4_printed_proposition_diverges.description: Tails where the claimants' printed propositions are NOT the same string (and their prop_digests differ), even though thm128 -- which digests the term, not its rendering -- collides. This is not a hash collision: it is the same term rendered under different notation in scope (nat vs omega, #+ vs +_omega, ZF_pairing_fm vs the fancy 'Pairing' bracket syntax, borel vs real_borel). 263 tails have 2 renderings, 1 has 3. Semantically safe, but it means the stored English can quote syntax that does not exist on the other side (see P5).
P4_printed_proposition_diverges.query: for each tail: select len({rec.prop for each new key's dump records}) > 1

examples.interpretation: The set code `ZF_pairing_fm` is a well-formed first-order formula. In other words, the code expressing the ZF unordered-pairing axiom belongs to the set `formula` of valid formula codes.

The formula `sep_ren(n,φ)` is obtained by applying the structural formula-renaming operation `ren` to `φ`, with both its source and target index bounds set to `7 + n` and its index map set to `rensep(n)`. Thus each free de Bruijn index below `7 + n` is replaced according to that renaming function.

Let `x` and `t` be natural-number de Bruijn variable indices. The formula asserting that `t` occurs in some finite repeated-general-union stage starting from `x`, and hence belongs to the epsilon-closure of `x`, has arity `succ(x) ∪ succ(t)`.

P5_text_quotes_syntax_only_one_claimant_.description: RECOMMENDED FOR RE-INTERPRETATION. Subset of P4: the stored English quotes, in backticks, an identifier that appears in only ONE claimant's printed proposition. A reader of the other claimant cannot find the quoted name at all -- e.g. the text explains `ZF_pairing_fm` but the Independence_CH rendering prints that constant as the bracket form. Dominated by Forcing / Independence_CH Internal_ZFC_Axioms and Transitive_Models / ZF-Constructible.
P5_text_quotes_syntax_only_one_claimant_.query: P4 tails where, for some new key k, (tokens in k's props) - (tokens in the other keys' props) intersects the backticked tokens of the interpretation

examples.interpretation: The set code `ZF_pairing_fm` is a well-formed first-order formula. In other words, the code expressing the ZF unordered-pairing axiom belongs to the set `formula` of valid formula codes.

If `p` is a well-formed first-order formula code, then the internal strong-replacement instance `ZF_replacement_fm(p)` is also a well-formed formula code. This includes the universal quantifiers that close all parameter variables beyond the first two positions reserved for the relation's input and output.
The set code `ZF_infinity_fm` is a well-formed first-order formula. In other words, the code expressing the ZF axiom of infinity belongs to the set `formula` of valid formula codes.

P6_file_pair_structurally_dissimilar.description: THE FILTER'S REAL BLIND SPOT, quantified. Tails where some differing shared-base-name theory pair has whole-file LINE-level similarity (difflib SequenceMatcher over non-blank whitespace-normalised lines) below 0.30, while the token-set Jaccard the existing filter uses is >= 0.30 and so never fires. Isabelle theory files in one domain share nearly all identifier tokens even when they are independent developments, so token-set Jaccard is far too generous: e.g. CSP_RefTK/HOL-CSPM DiningPhilosophers line=0.094, HRB-Slicing/Slicing JVMPostdomination 0.083, Abs_Int_ITP2012/HOL-IMP Abs_Int1 0.084, NREST/Refine_Monadic Refine_Foreach 0.104, HOL-Bali/HOL-MicroJava Type 0.113, Menger/Tree_Decomposition Graph 0.269. 373 tails from 15 theory pairs. NOTE: low file similarity does NOT imply a wrong copy -- Menger.Graph and Tree_Decomposition.Graph state the SAME record declaration verbatim, so their record-generated facts are one fact.
P6_file_pair_structurally_dissimilar.query: min over the tail's shared-base pairs of difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, lines(file A), lines(file B)).ratio() < 0.30

props: (⋀r. PROP ?P r) ≡ (⋀verts arcs more. PROP ?P ⦇verts = verts, arcs = arcs, … = more⦈)
examples.interpretation: A meta-level proposition about every extensible graph record is equivalent to the same proposition stated for records explicitly assembled from arbitrary component values. The components range independently over every vertex set, every set of ordered-pair arcs, and every extension value.
When the `prim_ty` recursor is applied to `Void`, it returns its first supplied result value. The other supplied results, corresponding to `Boolean` and `Integer`, are ignored.
For a natural number `N`, the assumption that `N` is greater than `1` implies that the locale predicate `DiningPhilosophers N` holds.

P7_declaration_text_differs.description: Tails where no declaration text is shared between the new keys: taking each claimant's position (file,line) and reading the command block that starts there (up to 14 lines, stopping at a proof keyword or a blank line), whitespace-normalised, the sets of blocks for the different new keys are disjoint. The complement is the strongest safety evidence available at scale: 10404 of 12230 (85%) share a byte-identical declaration block, i.e. the fact is stated verbatim in both places. 278 further tails have no usable position on at least one side (P8).
P7_declaration_text_differs.query: decl(pos) per claimant per new key; select intersection over new keys == {}

examples.interpretation: For an assignment to instance field `F`, declared in class `D`, using receiver expression `e₁` and right-hand-side expression `e₂`, the local variable at index `i` is classified as unmodified exactly when both expressions are classified as not modifying it. Both the receiver and assigned-value expression are therefore checked by `unmod`.

A boilerplate fact giving the runtime type-representation (used for reflection) of the type `prat`. It states that the type representation of `prat` is the term built from the type-name string "PosRat.prat" together with an empty list of argument types, reflecting that `prat` takes no type parameters.

P8_declaration_unavailable.description: Tails where at least one new key has no claimant with a resolvable source position, so the declaration-text check (P7) cannot run. Undecidable by textual means; needs the actual theory context.
P8_declaration_unavailable.query: some new key has no claimant with a (file,line) that resolves to a readable file

P9_english_explains_a_divergently_define.description: Tails where the interpretation explains, in backticks, a constant that occurs in the printed proposition AND whose declaration block is textually different in the two theories. Tier A = any textual difference (1502 tails); tier B = best-matching blocks differ with difflib ratio < 0.85 (451 tails, listed here). Precision is limited: the commonest cause is a `fun`/`datatype` block that merely GAINED cases or discriminator names on one side (CoSMed vs CoSMeDis, Jinja vs JinjaDCI), which leaves the specific equation unchanged. Use as a ranking, not a verdict.
P9_english_explains_a_divergently_define.query: tokens(prop) & backticked-tokens(interpretation) & {t : headindex(fileA)[t] != headindex(fileB)[t] and best difflib ratio < 0.85}

examples.interpretation: In every reachable system state `s`, the recorded visibility `vis s pID` of every post identifier `pID` is either friends-only visibility `FriendV` or public visibility `PublicV`. The selector `vis` retrieves the visibility value associated with a post identifier from the state.

The underlying partial function of the finite composition `x ∘⇩f xa` is the partial-function composition of `pfun_of x` with `pfun_of xa`. Consequently, an input is processed first by `xa` and then by `x`, with the composition undefined if either represented partial function is undefined at the required stage.

P10_prat_description_wrong_on_the_other_.description: CONFIRMED WRONG COPIES -- the one subpopulation where I verified the copied English is factually false about the entity it landed on. Combinable_Wands/PosRat.thy declares `typedef prat = {r::rat. r >= 0}` (NON-NEGATIVE rationals); CommCSL/PosRat.thy declares `typedef prat = {r::rat. r > 0}` (STRICTLY POSITIVE rationals; 0 is not a member). The two are different types with the same short name and the same operation names (pgte, pgt, padd, pmult, pmin, pmax, pdiv, pinv, half, pwrite), so a long list of algebraic lemmas prints identically. All 29 tails were interpreted from the Combinable_Wands side (old position is $AFP/Combinable_Wands/PosRat.thy for all 29) and 28 of the 29 texts literally say 'non-negative rationals'. Case B.3 copied those onto the CommCSL keys, where the claim is wrong. The existing filter cannot see this: token-set Jaccard is 0.645 and line similarity 0.645 -- the two files ARE nearly the same library; the divergence is one character (>= vs >). The 29th tail (028c9055dc7167f9c6644354b9f98b02, typerep_prat_def) says only 'the type prat' and is harmless.
P10_prat_description_wrong_on_the_other_.query: tails whose shared-base pair is [Combinable_Wands.PosRat, CommCSL.PosRat] and whose interpretation matches /positive|non-?negative|greater than zero|strictly/i

examples.interpretation: Characterizes the negation of the greater-than-or-equal relation on non-negative rationals. It states that `a` is not greater than or equal to `b` (negation of `pgte`) exactly when `b` is strictly greater than `a` (the `pgt` relation).

States that multiplication distributes over addition on non-negative rationals: `a` times the sum of `b` and `c` equals the sum of `a` times `b` and `a` times `c` (where `pmult` is multiplication and `padd` is addition).

States that adding the non-negative rational constant `half` (representing `1/2`) to itself yields `pwrite` (representing `1`). Here the addition is `padd`, the sum operation on non-negative rationals.

P11_claimants_are_genuinely_different_ob.description: Tails whose two claimants are, on inspection of the sources, genuinely DIFFERENT mathematical objects that merely share a short name -- the Term-vs-Term shape, missed by the filter. Adjudicated by reading the declarations of all 68 theory pairs whose same-named declarations differ. Verified pairs and their divergence: Combinable_Wands.PosRat|CommCSL.PosRat (prat is >=0 vs >0); IOA-ABP.Action|IOA-NTP.Action ('m action has 7 constructors incl. Next vs 10 incl. C_m_s/C_m_r/C_r_s/C_r_r); Abs_Int_ITP2012.ACom|HOL-IMP.ACom ('a acom: If has 4 args vs 6, While 4 vs 5, and strip/post/annos differ); HOL-Bali.Type|HOL-MicroJava.Type and .Value (ref_ty has NullT/IfaceT/ClassT/ArrayT vs NullT/ClassT); Jinja.Expr|JinjaDCI.Expr (expr_1 gains INIT/RI); CSP_RefTK.DiningPhilosophers|HOL-CSPM.DiningPhilosophers (RPHIL uses picks i (i-1) vs picks i ((i-1) mod N), DINING built from FORKs||PHILs vs FORKS||PHILS); HOL-MicroJava.SemilatAlg|Jinja(Threads).SemilatAlg and .LBVCorrect (acc has arity 1 vs 2 with a carrier-set restriction). IMPORTANT: for a tail to exist the printed proposition must be identical, which for genuinely different datatypes admits only constructor-agnostic BNF/derived boilerplate (rel_refl, set_finite, pred_mono, rel_map, in_rel, map_id0, size, distinct, exhaust, typerep). Those statements and their English are generic, so 326 of the 355 are harmless in practice; the 29 PosRat tails (P10) are the ones where the English asserts a property of the diverging definition.
P11_claimants_are_genuinely_different_ob.query: union of the tails of the manually adjudicated theory pairs listed in copied_divergent_pairs_tails.json

examples.interpretation: The operation `pred_action` is monotone with respect to pointwise implication between predicates. In detail, if `P ≤ Pa` means that every message satisfying `P` also satisfies `Pa`, then every action all of whose messages satisfy `P` also has all of its messages satisfy `Pa`.
As functions on annotated commands, `map_acom id` and `id` are equal. In other words, applying the annotation map with the identity function leaves every annotated command unchanged.

Assume that the natural number `N` satisfies `DiningPhilosophers N`, meaning `N > 1`. The complete dining-philosophers process `DINING N` is deadlock-free in the failures-divergences sense: all of its failures and divergence traces are permitted by the standard deadlock-free reference process over the full set of dining events.

_sample.description: Random sample read end-to-end against the Isabelle2025-2 and afp-2026-05-13 sources.
_sample.the_one_exception: 028c9055dc7167f9c6644354b9f98b02 -- PosRat.typerep_prat_def, Combinable_Wands.prat (>=0) vs CommCSL.prat (>0): different types, but the fact is the code-generator typerep boilerplate and its English says only 'the type prat', so the copy is not wrong. Its 28 siblings (P10) are wrong.
